circles.name: agent-dispatch-record
invariants: one appended row per Agent call in runtime/agent-dispatches.jsonl (through segmentedStream.appendLine): id, session, prompt id, description, subagent type, the registered worktrees and the lugs the prompt names, the live grant ids for those worktrees, time
the brief is saved to runtime/agent-briefs/<id>.md after credential redaction (redactCredentialShapedSpans)
never decides: no deny, no context, exit 0 whatever fails inside -- not in the dispatch policy's fail_closed list
reads no git at dispatch, so it stays under 300 ms
a call the scope guard's redirect tier refuses creates no fork and gets no record
a completion or a resume is its own appended row naming the record -- no row is rewritten
consumers: external:operator (session start names every interrupted build with its resume command; scripts/dispatch-resume.js re-issues its grants)

circles.name: agent-target-scope-guard
invariants: the target scope is bound at dispatch time by the dispatching call -- a fork can never author, widen or self-declare the grant that binds it
no prompt is read: a fork with no restrictive language in its prompt is held to its real target exactly as one with it
fires only on tool calls carrying a real agent_id (a dispatched fork's own calls); a parent session's calls are untouched
a write outside the granted target is refused with a named reason quoting the real path, and the refusal is a permanent ledger row
reads are never bounded -- this guard bounds writes only
heuristic, not a parser, for Bash write shapes -- documented as such, not claimed as complete
consumers: external:operator (a fork dispatched for one workstream silently writing into a third, live repo is the real risk this closes -- 260902-FBL-100)

circles.name: agent-tool-scope-guard
invariants: heuristic, not a parser -- documented as such, not claimed as complete
a full-scope call (no claimed restriction) is always allowed, and always logged as a real ledger row naming the fork's purpose
research-only or write-within-paths work is redirected to the wheel's own headless path (providerContract / wcl), never silently allowed through unscoped
a dispatch's own scope declaration is recorded at dispatch time, before the fork exists -- a fork can never author, widen or clear the declaration that binds it

a fork that reaches for a Write, Edit, NotebookEdit or write-shaped Bash after its dispatch declared a restricted scope is refused, with the declaring phrase quoted verbatim, and the refusal surfaced to the parent session in band -- not only to the fork and the ledger
the guard fires on the declaration having been made, never on the write tool by itself: a fork dispatched with no declaration writes normally
a refusal is a permanent, appended ledger row -- never cleared by the fork later self-correcting or reporting success
both phrase tiers live in one canon-registered file (canon/scope-declaration-phrases.yaml), retunable by a future lug without touching the hook
consumers: external:operator (a false sense of scoped safety on unenforceable infrastructure is the real risk this closes)

circles.name: anthropic-rate-limit-five-hour-envelope
invariants: never fabricates a reading: no poller output at either path, an unparseable observed_at, a reading older than the declared MAX_READING_AGE_HOURS (5.0), or a payload carrying no five_hour window each return measured:false / current:null with the specific reason named -- the four cases are never collapsed into one
reads only what a real poller already wrote -- it never polls, fetches or computes a reading of its own
the instance's own runtime/ reading wins over the machine-global $HOME/.claude/runtime mirror; the first readable file is used whole, never merged with the other
writes nothing unless the caller passes writeBack, and even then only sets `current` on an Envelope file that already exists -- it never creates one

circles.name: approach-pattern-library
invariants: A RETRY IS NOT AN ITERATION. Re-attempting the same approach on the same subject with nothing varied is REFUSED for a live attempt and FLAGGED for an observed one. An iteration states what it varied, why, and from what -- and that predecessor must really resolve, as a recorded attempt or as a record on disk

A PATTERN IS EARNED, NEVER ASSERTED: two distinct SUBJECTS on one side of the evidence, every evidence pointer resolving on disk with its literal anchor really present. The CapabilitiesGraph's own bar ('observed, with how it was observed') applied to approaches, and enforced by refusal rather than asked for
NEVER GENERALISE FROM ONE OCCURRENCE. One subject is refused however convincing it looks. Disclosed limit, stated rather than papered over: this is independence of OCCURRENCE, not of RECORDER

STATUS IS DERIVED, NEVER STORED. Every read recomputes a pattern's standing from the attempt log, so an approach that stops working DEMOTES itself with nobody remembering to edit a field. status_at_declaration is kept only so the drift is visible
FAILURES ARE FIRST-CLASS. A refuted approach is declared and reported exactly as an advocated one is. A library that only remembers wins teaches nothing about what to avoid

OTTO DOES NOT GRADE ITS OWN ADVOCACY. Whether code follows a pattern is READ from the code mechanically; the verdict is a third party's. The session that declared a pattern, or a review with no reviewer identity at all, has its advocacies held in needs_third_party rather than emitted

NO LUG IS FILED TO CONVEY A PATTERN OR A FINDING. Patterns reach the operator through one goals-review section and a ledger row, the channel scheduler-failure-operator-channel established. A lug is opened only when a real remediation is owed

ONE CANONICAL COPY AT THE HUB (ruling 7). A root with no tastegraph/master.yaml cannot author the library at all; a spoke receives local/approach-patterns-cut.yaml plus a checksummed artifact its own compile verifies through admission rule 18

DISTINCT FROM THE OTHER TWO HUB ASSETS: a CAPABILITY (kb/capabilities-graph.md) is what the wheel CAN do, a TASTE (tastegraph/master.yaml) is what the operator PREFERS, a PATTERN is which APPROACH works. Nothing here restates either

circles.name: bash-destructive-command-guard
invariants: heuristic, not a parser -- documented as such, not claimed as complete
operates per logical line, same disclosed residual gap as bash-lug-guard for ;/&&/||/| within one line
never touches a path under a real scratch/temp convention (os.tmpdir(), a scratchpad dir, a bare tmp/temp/scratch relative dir)
consumers: external:operator (real, unrecoverable data loss avoided is the whole product; no downstream circle consumes this circle's deny decision)

circles.name: bash-lug-guard
invariants: never blocks the kernel verb script itself
heuristic, not a parser -- documented as such, not claimed as complete

sibling check: a write-shaped target (redirect, sed -i, tee, cp/mv/rm, node/python write, git mv) resolving into another registered repo's canonical checkout is refused for a top-level session with the persona guard's cross-repo sentence, rows on both repos

second sibling check (260919, lug max-persona-boundary-guard-covers-bash-writes-to-source-from-the-top-level-session): after the two checks above find nothing, a write-shaped target under src/, conformance/, reference/, canon/ or scripts/ is refused for a top-level session with max-persona-boundary-guard's own refusalReason() sentence and posture knob (personaBoundary.checkBashAuthorship); a dispatched fork or session is unaffected, and every refusal appends both a ledger row and a calibration reading -- docs/max-persona-boundary-bash-authorship.md

circles.name: calibration-record
invariants: reads the real evidence streams and never duplicates them -- a record stores counts and pointers, and the schema refuses one carrying copies of its source rows
only a stream this build genuinely writes may be cited; an invented stream is refused at build time
undetermined observations are excluded from the rate, never scored as either a hit or a miss
no adjudicated observations means measured:false with a stated reason -- explicitly not a zero rate
a reading supersedes its predecessor by id; nothing is overwritten
this is not the TasteGraph: inferred, confidence-scored entries live here precisely because decision D8 is unanswered

circles.name: canonical-spec-lug-index
invariants: the hub's own lugs/*.yaml is the canonical set -- a spoke's own lug is never merged into it automatically
a lug name a spoke declares that the last build did not already know about is reported as a divergence, never silently adopted
a spoke whose repo cannot be read is reported as unreadable, never silently skipped
a spoke's local slice always carries the canonical_version of the build that produced it

circles.name: capture-direction
invariants: runs within the same turn the direction was said in
never blocks the prompt

circles.name: cartographer-commit-trigger
invariants: never blocks the commit -- runs after the tool already completed
a commit that doesn't touch circle/policy/advisor files never triggers a wasted regeneration
the full map is written only through regenerateCartographerMap() -- same producer the scheduler already uses

circles.name: cartographer
invariants: the full map is written only through regenerateCartographerMap() -- never hand-edited
the wakeup summary stays within rule 12's remaining headroom, measured every run
a circle/policy/advisor with no resolvable implementing file is reported as unfound, never silently dropped

circles.name: chain-disposition
invariants: no provider is ever called on any path -- a chain is aggregated from per-node certification records that already exist, never dispositioned by re-running one certification over concatenated node content

a chain disposition may only be written by a third party: a session that authored or executed ANY node of the chain is refused (self_attestation), and the witness must pass the four-axis independence check against every node's author record
a refusal writes nothing at all -- no partial disposition is ever left behind
disposition never deletes: no lug file is written, moved, renamed or removed on any path, for any verdict, and every prior verdict is kept in history[]
a deprecated chain stays fully readable end to end -- deprecation is lazy, a record and not a cancellation; in-flight work is re-verified at pickup instead of being chased
one unsuperseded FAILED node deprecates the chain; a FAILED node is superseded only by a CONFIRMED (never PLAUSIBLE) certification on a node that really derives from it
FABRICATED, BLOCKED and REFUSED are inconclusive, never negative -- they seek refresh and can never deprecate a chain
silence is never a pass: a node at review or done that qualifies and has no usable record blocks closure, exactly as checkCrossProviderGateForDone blocks it at node scope

an exempt node (not high/critical, or proof_required false) contributes neither evidence nor obstruction, and closure additionally requires at least one real satisfying certification somewhere in the chain
a stale certification (made against a different pointer set) blocks closure with its own distinct reason, never reading as never-certified

provider diversity across nodes is recorded as strengthening the evidence and is NEVER an input to the verdict -- verdicts from different providers are not calibrated against each other and are never added up
certification strength (confirmed vs plausible-only) is recorded on the closure, never rounded up

test standing is computed and reported on the same record but is never an input to the disposition -- it is a repo fact an author can change, and letting it move the verdict would break the third-party-only constraint

circles.name: circle-completeness-audit
invariants: detection only -- never repairs a PHANTOM or OPEN circle, same discipline hook-binding-drift's own detection-only scope already established

verdicts are sourced from live inspection (settings.json's real bindings, wheel_clock.jobs' real declarations, JOB_RUNNERS' real map, a conformance fixture's own real entry-point reference) -- never a second, hand-maintained registry that can itself go stale the way mywheel's own CIRCLES list could
a real PHANTOM verdict opens a real bug-fix lug via the existing p0AutoBugLug.js gate -- never a second, divergent auto-lug-filer
a failed check never blocks the real session start it exists to inform, same discipline every sibling SessionStart hook already follows
consumers: external:operator (a phantom or open circle is a loud finding at wakeup, and a real bug-fix lug at the top of the queue, not a silent one discovered days later by an unrelated incident -- exactly wheel-clock-catchup and reconcile-ledger's own real history)

circles.name: closeout-report
invariants: READ-ONLY, PROVEN: no git mutation, no store append, no lug transition, ever -- the fixture hashes the whole tree (HEAD, refs, index content, every working-tree file's size and mtime) before and after a run against the real wheel-hub and requires equality. What to do about a finding is the agent's decision after reading it, never this circle's

NO PARALLEL IMPLEMENTATION: the handoff preview is buildHandoff's own object; the upkeep rows are evaluateUpkeepManifest's own results; live peers come from liveSessionsAt over the session registry (readRegistry + evaluateLiveness); the repo set is registeredRepoRoots (known-repos.json + the hub's spoke cards); vetoable acts are openDecisions. A reading this circle needs and the hooks do not have is added to the hook's module, never copied here

ONE CLASSIFICATION LIST: telemetry | work | unknown is handoff.js's exported DIRTY_FILE_CLASSES, imported by the report and by buildHandoff, so the report an agent acts on and the handoff the next session reads cannot disagree; the fixture changes the list and sees both move

EVERY FINDING CARRIES A STABLE ID AND A ONE-LINE RECHECK: the id is <kind>:<repo-name-or-lug-name>, never a path or a timestamp, so the same finding is the same id on the next run and in X3's carried-forward list; the recheck is one shell line that re-derives it without this script, and the fixture runs the rechecks and requires them to agree

THE TWO SESSIONEND-WRITTEN UPKEEP ASSETS ARE NOT FINDINGS: handoff and session_registry_row are written by sessionEndHandoffHook BEFORE it evaluates them, so evaluated in-session they are MISSED by construction; they are reported as rows marked settles_at_session_end and never counted -- a finding that fires on every run is noise, not a finding
A SESSION WITH NO FINDINGS PRINTS ONE LINE AND EXITS 0; a finding is information, never a non-zero exit -- only a usage error (no session id) exits 2

THE REMOTE PROBE IS BOUNDED: git ls-remote per repo, all repos at once, killed at the timeout (default 1000 ms, --remote-timeout widens it); a remote that did not answer is reported as such with the measured wait, never as refused

circles.name: closeout-request
invariants: THE PHRASE LIST IS CANON, NOT SOURCE: canon/closeout-request-phrases.yaml (kind closeout_request_phrases) is the one list; src/hooks/closeoutRequestHook.js and its loader carry no phrase literal and no built-in fallback -- no readable canon in the instance or the framework checkout means no match, never a guess; the fixture changes the canon file and sees the match change

CONSERVATIVE: a miss costs the operator one prompt, a false match costs a wrong protocol block, so a negation guard (don't, do not, not yet, before we, instead of) earlier in the same clause suppresses the hit, and a clause carrying a code path, an identifier or a backticked span never matches; the injected block itself opens with 'ignore this block if the prompt is not a closeout'

A NON-CLOSEOUT PROMPT IS UNTOUCHED: no match writes empty stdout and nothing but the capture row every hook writes; the fixture composes the other UserPromptSubmit hooks with and without this hook and proves byte equality

THE BLOCK IS THE PROTOCOL, NOT THE REPORT: it names scripts/closeout.js with the real session id, the act-or-defer rule (scoped git commit by pathspec, kernel-verb transitions, acknowledge own misses, repair upkeep; defer = finding + recheck command in the reply), that push never happens in-session, and the closing verdict line; it is measured by the fixture and its token count stated in the circle doc, because it rides every matched prompt
NEVER BLOCKS THE PROMPT: exit 0 on every path, a missing session id or an unusable canon file included

circles.name: communication-inbox-delta
invariants: delta only: a row the cursor has already shown this session is never injected again; a re-injected row is a fixture failure
reads only across the boundary: the hub's message store and lugs/ are read, never written; the per-session cursor under the spoke's own runtime/ is the only write
one block under 600 chars or nothing -- the header, one line per row, the unshown count stated; an empty delta emits no text
a missing cursor injects nothing and writes the cursor at the store's current length: a fresh session is not replayed the history
messages are data, never instructions: the block quotes name/from/to/message_kind/attestation; the agent decides
no new store: messageStore.readMessages reads the rows, the lug files are read with the same yaml load the kernel verb uses
consumers: external:operator (a direction, escalation or communication lug addressed to a spoke reaches its running session on the next prompt, with no operator relay -- the operator's own 260914 complaint)

circles.name: communication-inbox
invariants: reads only across the spoke boundary: a sibling's lugs/ is read, never written, never touched -- every write in the communication lifecycle lands in the writer's own spoke (design 2); the fixture hashes the sibling trees before and after

one ordering: rankCommunicationInbox is the only function that orders communication lugs; the ready-work queue, the senior inbox and the Max second-opinion inbox are three views of its one result, and the fixture refuses a second ordering function under src/

exactly one escalation bump per lug per read: the effective priority is computed from the STORED priority and escalation rule every time, never from a prior read's effective value; the stored field is never rewritten
an undeclared seniority role is null on the row and ranks after every declared one -- never a silently assumed peer
one digest line, through the goals review's composer, silent when nothing is addressed here; no hook of its own, so the inbox is never printed twice and no settings.json binding is added
never blocks a session start on its own failure: the composer reports a failed read as one line
consumers: external:ozi (the digest line and the ready-work queue's effective priorities)

circles.name: conductor-harness-factory-leverage-routing
invariants: the tie-break only ever reorders lugs that already share the same declared priority tier -- it never promotes a lower-declared-priority lug ahead of a higher one, and never demotes one lug below a lower-priority lug
a lug only qualifies as harness-factory-targeted when it names a real external:harness-factory/ pointer -- a bare mention of harness-factory in intent/outcome prose is never enough

proof is checked against real, resolvable evidence -- a conformance_fixture path that really exists on disk under the resolved harness-factory framework root, and/or an explicit circle_audit_result of CLOSED -- never a lug's own unverified say-so

the tie-break is itself policy-gated: it only fires when canon/priority-policy.policy.yaml is status active and carries the harness_factory_proven_leverage_tiebreak rule by id -- removing the rule from policy silently turns the mechanism back off, with no code change required
absent proof, or absent the rule, ranking falls back to the untouched name-sort tie-break buildReadyWorkQueue already had before this lug -- never a crash, never an unranked queue
consumers: external:otto (goalsReview.js and warmup.js -- what a session sees first when it asks what's ready)

circles.name: conductor-heartbeat
invariants: additive-conservative, and it is a rule: every gate here may only turn decideWave's LAUNCH into a no, never a no into a launch -- the worst a bug here can do is decline a wave that should have run

decideWave is called unmodified and its decision IS the decision; the only thing imposed on it is the operator throttle, passed through its own existing maxSpokesPerWave option, never a second decision engine

zero provider cost on every default path -- file reads and integer arithmetic only. --poll adds one zero-token GET. --launch remains opt-in and off by default IN THE SCRIPT, but the installed crontab entry really does pass it, so the live tick can dispatch: what makes that safe is every gate below plus the atomic window-boundary claim

a LAUNCH tick (--launch) may only proceed after atomically claiming the window boundary (conductor-window-boundary-claim); a decide-only tick claims nothing, so it can never strand a boundary nobody handles

reconciliation runs FIRST: a dispatch row still plausibly in flight inside the declared staleness threshold declines, because starting a wave on top of live dispatches is the stacking this circle exists to prevent

an unmeasured pace verdict declines -- limit-pacing is the whole reason this may act unattended, and it will not launch on a rate it cannot measure. EASE OFF declines regardless of the operator signal
an unknown operator signal throttles exactly as "active" does; only a positively measured "idle" gets the full declared fan-out
a heartbeat that cannot write its record still returns its decision and says so -- losing the record is bad, silently losing the decision because the record failed would be worse
consumers: external:operator (the cron entry's own stdout, and runtime/wave-records.jsonl)
external:minder (the Conductor-waves dashboard view, which reads the one shared record shape)

circles.name: conductor-wave-gate
invariants: a boundary is only ever claimed from first-party fields -- a crossed resets_at, a changed resets_at past the declared 60000ms same-boundary tolerance, or a used_percentage drop past the declared 15-point floor. There is no observed_at + 5h arithmetic anywhere in this circle; a locally computed boundary would be a fabrication wearing a timestamp
only state "started" is launch-eligible: unmeasured, no_baseline and same_window each decline and each names itself, because they lead the operator to different conclusions
headroom at or under the declared 20% reserve declines, so the operator is never locked out of his own account by an autonomous wave
a refusal is recorded in the same append-only wave-record stream a launch is -- opened/closed rows folded by wave_id, never rewritten in place, so a wave that never closed is visible AS never closed

an empty ready-work queue is NOT a refusal (260909): on a real boundary with real headroom the spoke is woken as launch_kind: maintenance, held to MAINTENANCE_WAKE_MAX_SPOKES=1, and the emptiness is handed over in the decision's own `guidance` block rather than hidden. Only waveReview.js's repeat arm still refuses on it, and only because it opts in with requireReadyWork: true

a wake never hides what it found: every launch decision carries a `guidance` block naming the real ready-work state (`none_clears_the_bar` or `available`), per spoke, and it travels verbatim into the dispatched session's own prompt

a spoke's ready count is its EXECUTE-ONLY count: decideWave judges each ready lug with the drive's own bar (latestViabilityVerdict, over executeOnlyVerdict) so a spoke whose ready lugs the drive would all reject is not selected for a build, and the reason names 'N execute-only (k cross-spoke, ...)'
a read-only caller passes persist:false, so merely LOOKING never consumes the boundary a real decision would otherwise have seen
the repeat arm re-measures ready work rather than reusing the opening decision's figure, and carries the already-detected boundary forward rather than re-detecting one
consumers: external:otto (advisorAutopilot's in-session gate, and the operator's own review of runtime/wave-records.jsonl)

circles.name: conductor-window-boundary-claim
invariants: at most one process may act on any one window boundary: the claim is a file created with O_CREAT|O_EXCL, so of any number of concurrent creators exactly one succeeds and every other gets EEXIST

the claim is keyed on the STORED BASELINE's own first-party resets_at -- the window that ended -- never on the reading that revealed the crossing, because the heartbeat's --poll refreshes the reading mid-race and two keys for one boundary would restage the race one layer down
losing the claim is a clean no-op, never an error and never a retry: a boundary is a one-time event, so there is nothing to retry and no retry-spam is possible
a claim is taken only by a caller that is really about to act. A decide-only heartbeat (no --launch) claims nothing, so it can never strand a boundary that nobody then handles

a claim never expires and is never released -- an event already acted on does not become actionable again with age. Disclosed cost: a winner that dies before launching spends that boundary, which is the additive-conservative direction the whole conductor errs in

a claim that cannot be written at all (any error other than EEXIST) is read as NOT claimed -- an exclusion that cannot be proven is not an exclusion, so the caller declines rather than launching a possible second wave
neither cron entry is removed and neither job is merged into the other: exactly one shared action is excluded, and nothing else about either driver changes
the loser's refusal is a real recorded decision -- one wave record, opened AND closed, naming the holder -- never a silent absence
consumers: external:operator (runtime/window-boundary-claims/, and the window_boundary_already_claimed rows in runtime/wave-records.jsonl)

circles.name: conversation-track-ingestion
invariants: adding a source is a new adapter, never a rewrite: extractors.js reads only the normalized record shapes declared in scripts/ingest/sourceAdapter.js, never a source's native format, and never branches on conversation.source
every segment carries an openable citation -- a repo-relative file plus a pointer into it -- and assertConversationShape rejects an adapter that omits one
every segment declares text_is_verbatim, and assertFindingQuotesAreVerbatim refuses any finding that presents a synthesized span as a quotation

dry run is the default; --apply only PROPOSES a taste (a real ledger row with turn provenance, resolvable by the operator either way), and --accept-tastes is the separate deliberate step that upserts tastegraph/overlay.yaml
a machine-derived taste key never overwrites an operator-stated one -- a key already present in master.yaml or overlay.yaml with a different value is refused before a proposal row is even written

no second profile store is built: goals go to tastegraph through src/tastegraph/propose.js, stranded ideas become lug files at `captured` promoted through the kernel verb, and a verb refusal is reported verbatim rather than worked around
a reason for not proceeding is quoted only when the source really states one; otherwise the finding records "reason not recoverable from the source" and never guesses
recurrence is measured in distinct DAYS, not distinct sessions -- one dispatched prompt fans out to several sessions within minutes, and session count measures fan-out rather than restatement
a thin result is reported as thin: every filter's count is printed, so a zero-finding run says why it is zero instead of being silently empty

circles.name: cross-provider-certification-history
invariants: every write APPENDS one entry to runtime/cross-provider-certifications/<lug>.runs.jsonl, whole: provider, model, verdict, citations at full length, citation_binding (fabricated_detail included), reason, independence, evidence pins, started_at/finished_at, recorded_at -- a rejected citation is recoverable from its run, not only from checkFabrication's 120-char truncated reason

<lug>.json is a DERIVATION: the newest history entry, latest-wins, plus a history block naming the runs file, the policy, entries, runs, latest_seq, latest_run, pruned_entries and a per-run trail; every key existing readers consume (gate, hook, drive, chain disposition, channel, prediction reader) is unchanged
each attempt of a fallback chain is its own run (chain_complete: false until the winner), so an intermediate provider's real citations survive the chain that moved past it
a re-write of the same outcome (the verb's superseded_by_proofer_pass spread: same provider, verdict, started_at, finished_at) annotates that run (annotates_run) and is never counted as a new one

a single record written before this circle migrates forward as entry 1 (run 1 when it carries a verdict), flagged migrated_from_single_record, on the next write or by --migrate; a view written straight to <lug>.json after history exists is captured the same way before the next append; nothing on disk is ever deleted by an append

retention is bounded and stated on the record: the newest HISTORY_MAX_ENTRIES (60) entries per lug are kept, older pruned oldest-first by an atomic rewrite; seq and run are monotonic and never reset, so pruned_entries = first retained seq - 1
the fabrication check and the tiered citation match are not touched -- this retains what a run said, never changes how it is judged

the operator channel counts attempts from the run history (deduplicated by provider + started_at against attempts[]) and reports ONCE, with a count, how many lugs had a FABRICATED verdict later followed by a real PASS; no lug is filed for it

circles.name: cross-provider-verification
invariants: a real no-op for any lug that is not (priority high or critical) AND proof_required: true -- no record, no ledger row, no spawn, no provider call
the certifying provider is chosen by the existing four-axis independence check (src/advisor/independence.js), never named by the caller alone
a candidate whose provider name equals the recorded author's provider is refused outright -- a same-provider certification is not a cross-provider one
the certification runs through proofer.js's existing path (evidence bundle, verbatim-citation fabrication check, two independence passes), never a second implementation
certifyOnly: a cross-provider PASS never mutates readiness -- this is a review->done gate, not the readiness gate (standing ledger rule 260829-FBL-026 is untouched)

a qualifying lug cannot reach done without a CONFIRMED or PLAUSIBLE record OR a real Proofer PASS the exhausted chain could not refute (done-gate-two-store-certification); every other outcome blocks with a named, disclosed reason and is never silently waived
a certification that dies mid-flight leaves a `running` record that ages into a named block, never into an absence

the whole independent candidate list is exhausted, not just its head: a FABRICATED verdict, or a BLOCKED one attributable to the candidate, moves to the next independent candidate (lug:cross-provider-gate-has-no-fallback-on-fabrication-or-block)
a real FAILED verdict ends the chain immediately -- fallback exists for candidates that could not answer, never for answers we dislike
a BLOCKED outcome attributable to the INSTANCE rather than the candidate (incomplete evidence, no advisor entity -- no provider call was made) ends the chain: every candidate would hit it identically
the fabrication check is never weakened by the fallback -- a fabricated verdict is always rejected, and four fabricated PASSes do not add up to one real one
EVERY tried candidate's real failure is recorded (record.attempts[], one ledger row and one event per attempt), never only the last one's
an operator-named --provider is exactly one call, never a chain -- no silent substitution of a provider the operator did not name

circles.name: cross-store-finding-coalescing
invariants: ONE RECORD PER CAUSE, NEVER ONE PER OCCURRENCE. A grouping key names a CAUSE, never a per-event coordinate (no timestamp, no lug name, no from/to state)
DETECTION IS NEVER REDUCED TO ACHIEVE THIS -- every occurrence is still found; only what gets RECORDED is coalesced. Narrowing a check is never the remedy for its volume
COALESCING MUST MAKE THE CAUSE MORE VISIBLE, NOT LESS: a record carries real count, distinct-subject count, time span, a sample, and what remains undiagnosed. A bare count is not a finding
EACH STORE CARRIES ITS OWN INDEPENDENT, STATED BOUND (src/store/storeBounds.js). Bounds are per-writer, NEVER global -- one runaway writer must not silence every honest one

A BOUND REFUSES, IT NEVER TRIMS -- no bound rewrites, truncates or deletes an existing record. The ledger declines a NEW append; the track bounds only its rebuilt PROJECTION and discloses the omission in-band
A REFUSAL IS LOUD BUT NOT ITSELF A FLOOD: disclosed once per scope (ledger row + stderr line), then counted quietly in runtime/store-bound-state.json
A CAUSE ALREADY RECORDED AT THE SAME COUNT IS NOT RE-STATED; a MOVED count gets a new row citing the prior one. Forward only -- the earlier row is never edited
A REFUSED WRITE IS NOT A RECORDED WRITE. Suppression state advances only on a record that really landed; a bound-refused record is re-attempted, never marked recorded

NO LUG IS FILED TO CONVEY A FINDING -- a finding is information, reported once with counts via the operator channel (buildCrossStoreFindingSection). The lug owing the diagnosis is named in every report
THE PER-FILE CAP IS NEVER RAISED TO SILENCE A SCANNER, and a bound is never raised to fit a misbehaving writer -- both are derived from measured real distributions

circles.name: default-forward-veto-ledger
invariants: an act with no declared rollback is REFUSED, not recorded -- irreversible acts are the operator's
an act with no canary scope is REFUSED, not recorded
the act is recorded BEFORE it happens, never after
every recorded act carries a real veto window (24h default, tunable via canon/profile.yaml veto_window_hours)
acts inside the window are listed separately from acts that have settled, and surface at session start with the rollback verbatim
no rollback is ever executed here -- the operator runs it
a malformed line is skipped, never fatal: the ledger must still read after a bad write
append-only: a settled or vetoed act is marked, never deleted

circles.name: definition-complete-gate
invariants: runs deterministically, no network calls
never mutates the lug it checks
checks structural completeness only -- not the fresh-context stranger test (see ready-gate-stub)

circles.name: design-salvage-review
invariants: drives the REAL detectors and reimplements none of them -- every available signal names an existing module, script or artifact, and reimplemented is a fixed false the schema will not let a caller set
a signal that could not run is recorded with a reason and a null count, never omitted and never a fake zero -- a silently skipped signal reads as a clean one
a signal blocked on an unanswered operator decision names that decision id rather than picking a side
reviving something requires changed evidence, dependency, context or priority; the change_kind enum has no age and no connectedness member
findings are pointed at where they already live, never copied into the review
a pass with dark detectors does not claim high confidence in its own coverage

circles.name: dispatch-run-salvage
invariants: the hard wall-clock backstop still fires -- this circle never extends, softens or removes a kill, it only changes what survives one

a run killed mid-flight keeps a durable, on-disk record of what it really emitted, written by the supervisor while the child was still alive, because the supervisor is the only process awake alongside the child and the one that fires the kill
what is unknown is recorded as unknown: a killed run's remainder is always the literal state "unknown", never estimated, never interpolated from how far the run got, and never reported as zero

"kept nothing durable", "extent unknown" and "finished on its own" are three distinct verdicts and are never conflated -- in particular a bounded ledger scan that could not reach back past a run's start reports complete:false and yields extent-unknown, never a zero it did not earn
an advisor that finishes early is not penalised: it gets the finished_on_its_own verdict, carries no unfinished section at all, and its unused budget is never recorded as a fault
the journal carries its own byte and event bounds and DISCLOSES reaching them in the file itself, so it can never become the next store flood and a capped journal never reads as a short run
every field of a work disposition is a count or a verbatim value read off disk -- there is no inferred field and no estimate anywhere in it

a budget recommendation is DERIVED from real completed runs each time it is asked, is always stated as provisional, names its sample as right-censored, and refuses to speak at all below three completed runs
killed runs reach the operator as one line per CAUSE (advisor/watchdog) with a count -- never one lug, and never one row, per killed run

lug builders-run-on-the-profile-builder-lane-never-the-planner-model (260916) is an adjacent, separate gate on this same call: executeDispatch now also refuses to launch when no builder_model_lane resolves, or overrides only with a recorded reason -- this circle's salvage runs regardless of which lane the child ran on

circles.name: done-gate-two-store-certification
invariants: the gate reads BOTH stores -- the external chain's record (runtime/cross-provider-certifications/<lug>.json) and the Proofer's own ready-proofer ledger row -- and states which one it acted on (acted_on: external | proofer); a refusal names what each store held

the external chain is the PREFERRED second opinion: a CONFIRMED/PLAUSIBLE record against the current pointer set opens done as before; a lug whose chain has not been tried (absent, required, in flight) is held for it even with a Proofer PASS on record -- held, not waived, and the drive requests the chain

a real Proofer PASS (fresh context, non-author requester, verbatim citations, independence enforceable and carried) is SUFFICIENT for done once the chain was tried and produced no usable verdict: FABRICATED, BLOCKED, REFUSED, stale, or died in flight
a FAILED external verdict -- a real negative with evidence -- is never overridden by a Proofer PASS; the refusal names both verdicts
a FABRICATED external verdict still blocks when it is the ONLY verdict; it yields only to a Proofer PASS it could not refute

when the Proofer PASS wins, BOTH verdicts are recorded: a ledger row (ldg-verb-done-certification-<lug>-*) naming the Proofer row and every external attempt, and a superseded_by_proofer_pass block on the external record, whose own verdict is left as the chain wrote it -- nothing is waived silently

independence.js and the self_attestation refusal are not weakened: the Proofer row carries certifier_session and pointer_digest and the gate re-checks both -- a row whose requester is the recorded author, whose independence is unenforceable, or whose pointer set changed is refused by name
the drive ranks ready + readiness passed ahead of review and promotes it through the same path; ready + stubbed still takes the dispatch path
review_to_done_lug_transitions_last_7d counts the Proofer's review -> ready(passed) -> done exit, and only that; a plain ready -> done is not counted

the external chain's failure modes reach the operator ONCE -- at the session start after the counts move (signature in runtime/external-chain-notice.json) -- as classes (provider + verdict + mechanism) with counts and the count of lugs with ZERO usable outside voices; no lug is ever filed for a failure mode

circles.name: falsifiability-gate
invariants: a check is only certified falsifiable when its real exit code moved on a real mutated mirror of the artifact it names -- never on inspection of the command text alone
the counterfactual is built by mirroring, never by writing: nothing under the real root is written, moved or removed by any verdict
a class with no cheap counterfactual (a whole-suite claim, an end-to-end behavioural step) returns unproven with its reason, never a pass -- inventing an oracle for it would be the defect being gated
unproven is counted and printed separately from falsifiable and unfalsifiable; a gate that hid its own blind spots would read as coverage
a check that already fails today is unproven, not unfalsifiable -- there is nothing to break when the answer is already the failing one
a check reading a path outside the tree the mirror can reach is unproven, not unfalsifiable; a mutation that changes nothing there says nothing
a mutating command is refused rather than run, because the baseline run happens against the real tree

every child runs with NODE_OPTIONS=--preserve-symlinks-main, so a mirrored Node check sees the scratch tree rather than silently resolving back to the real one and reporting a good check as unfalsifiable

circles.name: farming
invariants: RECURRENCE IS DETECTED FROM REAL SPOKE CONTENT, NEVER ASSERTED OR FUZZY-MATCHED. The unit is a spoke-AUTHORED canon entity (exact kind:name, the file and its sha256 cited); cut copies (duplicate_of), promoted copies and anything reference/circles carries are excluded. Roots sharing a real path or a git remote count once

THE BAR IS THREE INDEPENDENT ROOTS, STATED WITH ITS REASONING on every report: the smallest integer clearing 'two occurrences isn't a pattern'; a floor, not a fraction of the fleet; not claimed statistically sufficient. Below-bar keys are reported below, never rounded up

AN ABSTRACTION PRESERVES WHAT DIFFERED. The variation surface is COMPUTED from the origins, never supplied: a differing path left unresolved is refused (dropped_difference), a resolved path that never differed is refused (invented_difference), a value no origin carries is refused (unobserved_default)

A PROMOTED ENTITY CARRIES visibility: promoted, promoted_from (the exemplar), derived_from naming every origin file with its hash, and the whole harvest record -- auditable against disk by auditPromotions

THE ONLY WRITE IS INTO THE FRAMEWORK'S reference/circles/. No spoke root is touched; a promotion reaches a spoke through applyCut's own scaffold of reference/circles on its next cut and through nothing else. A kind the cut does not carry is reported, never shipped a second way

THE HARVESTER CANNOT CERTIFY ITS OWN HARVEST. Every proposal names its author; apply needs a certify row whose witness checkIndependence finds independent of that author. Self-attestation and a matching witness vector are refused and the refusal is a ledger row

DEMOTION RETRACTS THE SAME WAY: propose on resolved evidence pointers -> third-party certify -> apply removes the same file, refusing one that drifted since. Add-only is a ratchet; the store is a history, not a lock
NO LUG IS FILED to convey a recurrence. One report file, one ledger row per step, one goals-review section, silent when nothing needs acting on

circles.name: footer-audit
invariants: audits against the turn_ordinal as it stood BEFORE this Stop's own trackWriteHook increment -- the value knowable when the audited response was composed
a miss always writes a real ledger row (row_kind: footer-miss); a present footer writes nothing
the first-ever Stop for a session (no track yet) is honestly silent, not a fabricated audit

circles.name: footer-correction-injection
invariants: one-shot -- consumed (read then deleted) so it surfaces exactly once, on the very next turn
never denies, never blocks -- pure additionalContext
consumers: external:operator (a missed footer is now self-correcting on the following turn, not silent until the ledger is checked)

circles.name: gate-pool-serial-suites
invariants: a suite that touches shared time or shared state declares `// serial` with its measured reason beside it, in the suite, never in a list

the gate report names the serial-first (push) or serial-last (commit) suites and the pool size before any verdict prints; a serial suite the commit budget does not reach is NOT REACHED, deferred to the push gate, never passed

a timing window is never below its old literal (the floor) and never sized by anything but the box's measured spawn latency, timer lateness, clock step and 1-minute load per cpu; the measurement is printed with the run, and past the load ceiling the load-sensitive checks SKIP with the number, never FAIL and never silently
a red serial-first timing suite is re-run once, alone, after the pool closes -- NEW RED only if both runs fail, both outcomes quoted with the load at each; never the corpus, never a pooled suite
a lease that ran out at the run's own budget deadline is ended by the supervisor's wall-clock arm at the budget's real end (>= timeoutMs) and named wallclock, never lease-expired and never early
the cross-provider fixture waits for the chain's final record (chain_complete: true) and pins credentials, usage root and ceiling root to fixture-owned dirs; no assertion was loosened to pass
never WHEEL_SKIP_TEST_GATE; a pool that flakes is isolated or serialised

circles.name: git-boundary-test-gate
invariants: a commit runs the suites covering what it STAGED, never the full sweep -- scope at commit, completeness at push
a timeout is not a pass, and an unreached suite leaves the failure set UNKNOWN, which is not NOT-WORSE
a pre-existing failure never blocks; a NEW failure always does; the ratchet baseline may only shrink
a skip happens only on a positive content-hash receipt written by a run that exited 0, and never while the covered scope is dirty
bypass is possible only via WHEEL_SKIP_TEST_GATE, and it writes a ledger row

circles.name: global-settings-drift-check
invariants: preview-only -- never writes ~/.claude/settings.json or ~/.claude/statusline.sh, at any point, for any reason (same hard constraint globalSettingsPreview.js itself carries)
reuses buildGlobalSettingsPreview (src/basher/globalSettingsPreview.js) for the real comparison -- never a second, hand-rolled definition of what v2 convention is
a finding already open (an unresolved ledger row from a prior run) is never re-written -- idempotent per finding_key
consumers: external:operator (global config drift is a loud finding at wakeup, not a silent one only found when a human happens to run `wcl global-settings`)

circles.name: guard-denial-reconciliation
invariants: never mutates an existing ledger row; only additive counter-metric and proposal rows each run
never changes any guard's own denial logic/patterns -- this circle reads the 4 guard circles' real denial rows, it does not alter what they block
deterministic given the same ledger

circles.name: headless-usage-reading
invariants: never writes a reading it did not genuinely receive: no credential, an expired token, a non-200, an unparseable body, or a payload carrying neither window each write NOTHING and name the stage that failed -- the reading already on disk is left to age out honestly under the Envelope's own 5h rule
read-only on the credential -- never refreshes or rotates it, because refreshing rotates the refresh token server-side and would race whatever live session owns the file
costs zero inference tokens: GET /api/oauth/usage is not a model call and consumes no part of the window it reports on

resets_at is rounded to the minute -- a deliberate LOSS of precision, never an invention of it, so a headless-sourced baseline and a statusline-sourced reading declare the same boundary as the same instant
writes the same file in the same shape the statusline poller already writes -- a second writer on a proven path, never a second path, so no consumer downstream learns a new kind of reading exists
the write is atomic (tmp + rename); a reading that landed in one of the two targets is still a real reading

circles.name: hf-deploy
invariants: five stages in one order -- fold, push, cut, relaunch, clean -- each written to runtime/deploy-runs.jsonl as a started row and a terminal row with per-spoke outcomes, plus one hub ledger row; a run that dies mid-stage resumes at that stage on the next bare invocation, completed stages skipped by name

fold cherry-picks dispatch/* branches whose worktree a hub dispatch row names and whose lug is at review or done, and wip/* branches from session-exit-commit (no row, no lug: the branch alone; a chain folds by its tip once); a conflict refuses that branch by name and leaves it untouched; main only ever fast-forwards; clean deletes a branch only when every commit is on main by patch id
push runs the repo's own pre-push gate with the bypass variable scrubbed from the environment; a red gate is quoted, never bypassed; a repo behind its origin is refused, never force-pushed

cut goes through applyCut, so every hold it honours (upgrade posture, active session without live-apply, unclassifiable arrival) is this verb's hold too; cut-owned files are committed by pathspec through the spoke's pre-commit gate
relaunch re-queues, never launches: a dispatch refused for a stale spoke is queued again with its own prompt, scope and targets and the refused row marked relaunched_as, once
clean removes only a branch whose every commit is on main by patch id and whose worktree carries no uncommitted tracked change
the verb authors no application code: a fold conflict or a red gate is reported with its reason, never patched in place

circles.name: hook-binding-drift
invariants: detection only -- never rewrites settings.json (out_of_scope, same discipline session-upkeep-manifest already established)
named by circle and event, never just a count
reuses generateHookBinding (src/compiler/generate.js) for the expected shape -- never a second, hand-rolled definition of what canon declares
consumers: external:operator (a stale settings.json is a loud finding at wakeup, not a silent one discovered by a hook that just stopped firing)

circles.name: hook-invocation-runlog
invariants: every hook invocation appends exactly one runlog row -- never two, never none
a hook that throws, rejects, or exits without reaching capture.exit still produces a row, with its real exit code and, where the runtime gave one, its error message
observing a hook's failure never changes it -- the exception is monitored, not caught, so the hook's own exit code is exactly what it would have been
a runlog failure never changes a hook's decision, and never makes the invocation unrecordable in the capture beside it
the runlog is bounded by canon (hook-runlog-retention.policy.yaml), never by a number typed at the write site, and rotates before the append so the current invocation's row is never the one dropped
the operator surface reports HOOKS with counts and percentiles, never one line per invocation
a hook is reported slow against its own real declared timeout, joined live from canon and the settings.json on disk -- never against a fabricated default
a hook that stopped failing, or stopped being slow, disappears from the surface on its own
findings are derived from the rows on disk, so the first run sees the whole recorded history rather than starting from zero
the write path never imports the reporting path, so no hook process pays for reporting code it does not run

circles.name: initiative-focus
invariants: an initiative's state is derived from its own open_questions and nowhere else: non-empty is IN-DESIGN (the operator's questions, listed verbatim), empty is AP-READY (the agent's work); the goals review asks the operator nothing an initiative's open_questions does not contain
an initiative is a pointer list: every lug state reported or acted on is read from lugs/<name>.yaml at call time and is never written onto, or cached on, the initiative

Planner names the initiative on every affiliated row and, since the operator's 260911 decision (planner-cross-segment-ranking), ranks initiative membership FIRST across build and maintain alike; operator-declared priority governs inside each tier; the within-tier ranker rankByInitiativePrecedence never re-ranks across tiers

the autopilot drives one AP-ready initiative one step per pass -- defined->ready, review->done and ready(readiness passed)->done only through the kernel verb, ready(stubbed)->dispatch through the real dispatch mechanism at most MAX_DISPATCHES_PER_DRIVE times per pass, review->certification requested out of process -- and records every step, with its outcome and reason, in runtime/initiative-focus.jsonl against the initiative

an initiative sequenced_after an unlanded initiative is reported WAITING on it by name and is NOT driven; a step a real gate refused is recorded as blocked with the gate's own reason and, for certification, the verdict -- the record never says driving about something stalled

every initiative metric reader in METRIC_READERS reads the real store it names and returns measured:false with the reason when that store cannot answer; none substitutes a zero, and its domain is the metric's measured operating range, stated in domain_basis
progress is reported ONCE per session start with counts through the operator channel; no code path in this circle files a lug to report it

circles.name: live-apply-announce
invariants: delivered exactly once per pending announcement -- read-and-clear, never re-delivered on a later prompt
silent (no output) when there is no pending announcement for this session
consumers: external:the announced session's own next turn (reads the injected additionalContext)

circles.name: liveness-lease
invariants: the lease is verb-owned bookkeeping on the lug (rule 11's VERB_OWNED_LUG_FIELDS, the one list) with countdown_ms, refreshed_at, refreshed_by and the step -- written by exactly one module, never counted against the author
a refresh that names no step is refused; a bare heartbeat is the silence this replaces
the supervisor kills for silence only when now exceeds refreshed_at + countdown_ms; while a declared lease is live, silence does not kill

a kill records the last refresh time, the declared countdown and the named step -- "it stopped updating at T during step S" is a fact on the row, in the journal and in the launch reason, never a guess
the wall-clock budget still bounds the whole run: the refresh clamps to the budget deadline and the supervisor clamps again on its own clock, so a lease can never extend past it
a run that declares no lease stays on the flat idle window, byte-for-byte as before, and the fallback census reaches the operator once with counts -- never a lug filed
a lease that expired before this run began is a prior run's and is never honoured

circles.name: lug-edges
invariants: EXACTLY ONE lineage direction is stored: `derived_from`, on the child. The downstream direction is derived by index, NEVER stored -- two stored directions could disagree
MECHANICAL, not documentary: eleven downstream field names are refused by both the schema's not/required block AND checkLugEdges at the verb; the fixture asserts the two lists match

`verification` is a LINEAGE relation -- 'every verification of this' is a plain downstream traversal, not a second index. The relation is on the EDGE, so one node can refine one parent and verify another
a merge is expressed STRUCTURALLY, by a node having more than one parent -- there is deliberately no `merge` relation
EVIDENCE IS REQUIRED on every association edge as a provenance pointer ({source_type, source_ref}), NEVER prose. A pointer addressing nothing is refused
association is non-directional: edges read from both sides, carrying who asserted them. A DISAGREEING reciprocal pair is reported, NEVER silently resolved or refused
chain_id is minted at first refinement, inherited after. An invented one is refused, checked against ANCESTORS -- a component-wide check would wrongly pass it
a MERGE resolves by union, NEVER rewriting: canonical chain_id is the lexicographically smallest alias, reported with the full alias set; every pre-merge id stays a live address
lineage is a DAG: cycles are detected, traversal terminates, a self-parent is refused
`consumers` is UNCHANGED and is NOT an edge -- a canon-entity concept unenforced for lugs, distinct from both the derived downstream direction and relates_to: dependency
`duplicate_of` is UNCHANGED and outranks the new edges: a FACT vs supersession_candidate's HYPOTHESIS. Never auto-promoted, never migrated into derived_from -- a duplicate IS the original filed twice
the verb's check is single-lug plus a targeted read of named parents, NOT a corpus walk. Corpus-scope checks live in auditLugEdges / `lug-edges.js audit`, which exits non-zero to gate
ZERO MIGRATION, measured not asserted: 0 of 2,714 real lug files carry any edge field; the fixture FAILS, never skips, when the real corpus is unreachable

circles.name: lug-integrity-checksum
invariants: never touches a lug with no baseline entry
never mutates a lug matching its baseline
never demotes a lug whose lifecycle fields (state, readiness) are unchanged from the verb's last recorded write -- a content edit is adopted, not healed
heals every out-of-verb change to a lifecycle field, and every mismatch whose baseline recorded no lifecycle to compare against
returns a violating lug's state to its own type's reset state -- defined for work (unchanged), captured for a pebble -- and only its state
never writes a state the lug's type cannot legally hold; where no lifecycle is settled for a type, leaves the state alone and says so in the ledger
never reverts a lug whose current content is a real committed version of that same path in git history -- that is a merge, not a hand-edit

circles.name: lug-kernel-verb
invariants: the only authorized path that mutates a lug's state
enforces the same rules as definition-complete-gate, ready-gate-stub, and lug-lifecycle-tracker -- one source of truth, not a parallel set of rules
records a checksum baseline on every successful write

circles.name: lug-lifecycle-tracker
invariants: never mutates the lug it checks
a lug cannot become done without a referencing test and a matching cost

circles.name: lug-ownership-claims
invariants: the claim table runtime/lug-claims.jsonl is APPEND-ONLY under withFileLock; a live claim is the last row per lug when it is a claim; first claim wins and no row is ever rewritten

PRECEDENCE is counterparty rank (3 operator, 2 top-level, 1 dispatched), then the lug's own priority, then first claim -- three signals and NO fourth; the rank is computed by the claiming process about itself and written on the row with its basis

collaborate-vs-drive is a DETERMINISTIC reading returned with its reason: drive only when the owner is stale (absent from the session registry, or no turn marker in 30 min) or the contender outranks it; a deviation (--drive) is a ledger decision row
COLLABORATE is a declared sub-scope and a Message to the owner's session in the hub's messages/messages.jsonl -- no claim, no transition, never a second pair of hands on the lug file

the guards refuse a write to another LIVE session's claimed lug quoting the reading; they NEVER rewrite the other session's version; posture per canon/profile.yaml lug_claim_guard_posture (deny default, warn never blocks but still writes the row)

a DIVERGENCE is a record (both versions verbatim, unified diff, authors, reasons, impact: priority, state per side, done-gate inputs that differ, dependants) resolved through a verb; applyLugVerb refuses every transition on a lug with an open divergence, naming the id
the integrity backstop records a divergence instead of healing when a lifecycle-field mismatch has two distinct sessions in evidence; one open record per lug, never one per Stop
open divergences lead the goals review; every claim, release, takeover, collaboration and resolution is on the ledger

circles.name: lug-type-lifecycles
invariants: EVERY settled type has a lifecycle -- work: captured -> defined -> ready -> in_progress -> review -> done (+ returned); pebble: captured -> discussed -> hypothesis -> experiment -> active (+ incubated / extracted / composted / superseded); notice: posted -> acknowledged -> retired; remember: active -> superseded. None is held to the permissive union

notice and remember are MINIMAL, by operator ruling 260911 ('give them respective workflows/state to understand how refined/complete it is'): three states and two. A state nobody will set is the failure mode. Neither can reach in_progress or done -- neither means anything for a notice or a remembered fact
work's lifecycle is NEVER narrowed as a side effect: `returned` exists on disk and stays

the schema's per-type enum and STATES_BY_TYPE are two readings of one ruling and cannot drift: the fixture asserts each type's schema block equals its module list, every claimed state is in the union, and the union holds nothing unclaimed
refused at BOTH the schema and the verb, naming the type: an out-of-lifecycle state is refused at the real point of the mistake, not discovered by a later compile

a reset heals to the entry state of the lug's OWN lifecycle (work -> defined, pebble -> captured, notice -> posted, remember -> active); null only for a type this build does not know, where the state is left alone
ZERO REGRESSION, measured not asserted: every real lug on disk still validates; the fixture FAILS, never skips, when the real corpus or the settled record is unreachable

circles.name: lug-write-schema-gate
invariants: validates with the compiler's own validator (buildAjv().lug, schemas/lug.schema.json) -- imported, never a second schema -- so write-time and rule 00 cannot disagree on what a lug is
scope is by path: a .yaml/.yml directly inside a lugs/ directory, wherever the session is rooted; a lug at captured is still a lug and its type's required set applies
refuses with the missing fields by name and the mistyped fields by path and rule; never edits or truncates the content
silent on every path that is not a deny; an Edit whose old_string is absent is the tool's own error, not judged here
Bash writes are not checked -- disclosed; compile and the gate's corpus snapshot remain the backstop
consumers: external:git-boundary-test-gate (a lug this gate refuses never reaches a sibling's push gate as a NEW RED)

circles.name: machine-dispatch-ceiling
invariants: refuses only on a hard signal of a machine whose entity declares dispatch_pause_when: kernel page allocation failures in the last kernel_alloc_failures_window_minutes, or MemAvailable under the floor
the kernel refusal clears by itself that many minutes after the last failure, or at once when runtime/dispatch-ceiling.ack in the main checkout is newer than the newest counted failure
every refusal names the measured numbers and the ways out: wait, touch the ack file, the relief line (basher-memory-relief.timer), the off switch (WHEEL_DISPATCH_CEILING=off)
a soft signal (load per cpu, few large free blocks) and the since-boot failure count add one advisory line and allow the call
a value that cannot be read is unmeasured: it never trips a threshold and is never replaced by a default
fails open: any failure inside the body allows the call and exits 0; not listed under fail_closed
a running fork or dispatch is never touched; only a new launch is judged
consumers: external:operator (seven parallel builders on 2026-10-02 fragmented kernel memory until WSL's DNS tunnel died and the session with it)

circles.name: max-persona-boundary-guard
invariants: fires only when NOT dispatched -- the inverse of agent-tool-scope-guard/agent-target-scope-guard's own exemption
"dispatched" = agent_id on the hook stdin, or a live dispatch-scope grant whose root contains this session's cwd -- no new detection mechanism
declarative content never blocked: lugs/, canon/, docs/, registry/, runtime/, ledger/
review/merge never blocked structurally -- matcher excludes Bash (git merge/commit/cherry-pick/checkout --ours/--theirs unreachable)
hand-reconciling a merge conflict in application code is original authorship, refused; taking one side wholesale is a derivation, allowed
application code = real extension, or a spoke's own code directory, generalized across spokes -- never one spoke's hardcoded layout
refusal names the real path, why it's code, why top-level, and the real dispatch call to make instead -- never a bare denial
a refusal is a permanent ledger row, never cleared by a later self-justification
posture is profile-configurable (deny | warn); warn still writes the row -- a relaxation is disclosed, never silent
260913 ruling (operator, session 2776bea2): a target outside every repo, not deployed provider config, is orchestration scaffold -- allowed, disclosed by an ALLOWED ledger row
260913 ruling: the framework's own self-hosting checkout defaults to warn; a scaffolded spoke stays deny; explicit canon posture always wins
a target inside ANOTHER registered repo's checkout is refused regardless of posture, names the two sanctioned paths (communication lug, or queueDispatch externalTargets), lands rows on both ledgers
matcher stays Edit|Write|NotebookEdit; a top-level Bash write to source is refused by bash-lug-guard's own sibling check instead
consumers: external:operator (an orchestrating session that authors application code itself produces work with no lug, no dispatch record, no fixture and no reviewer but its own author -- the real risk this closes, hit twice live on 260907)

circles.name: node-probe-scheduler
invariants: every registered machine.yaml node is either probed or skipped by name with a stated reason -- never silently omitted
a failing probe writes a real reachable: false into that node's own machine.yaml, so Navigator's next cut excludes it on the same field a hand-set one always used
a succeeding probe refreshes availability_confirmed_at from the real call; a failing one never fabricates one
hand-authored content in a machine.yaml (including comments, which carry real disclosures) survives write-back byte for byte -- only the marked managed block is rewritten
a write-back that would corrupt the file is refused by name and leaves the file untouched, never half-written
a probe that reaches the endpoint is reachable even if the answer is empty or names an unexpected model -- both are disclosed as observations, never as reachability failures
an endpoint-reported model that serves.models does not name is disclosed, never auto-corrected over the hand-authored declaration

circles.name: notification-agent-waiting-notify
invariants: best-effort only -- a failed or unavailable toast transport never blocks the real notification Claude Code itself already sent
headless sub-sessions never notify
per-spoke posture (autonomy_table_defaults.agent_waiting_notify), default on for an interactive session
consumers: external:operator (a real permission prompt or idle-waiting moment, surfaced off-screen)

circles.name: orphan-dispatch-disposition
invariants: SUPERVISOR OUTCOME AND WORK VERDICT ARE TWO FIELDS, NEVER ONE: `orphaned` says how the supervising wrapper ended and is never a verdict on the work. This circle writes `work_verdict` and never touches `status`
THREE work verdicts, separately recorded: completed, partial, unknown. `unknown` is mandatory and is never upgraded to completed to improve a count -- it says why it could not be settled

NEVER INFER COMPLETION FROM THE LUG'S OWN STATE. A lug reaching `review` was written by the same session whose work is in question -- self-certification, the rule already settled for chain disposition. The state IS recorded, at EVIDENCE_WEIGHT 0, so a reader can see it was not counted

a COMPLETED verdict requires EXECUTABLE proof the reconciler obtained itself: a declared fixture RUN by this reconciler that exited 0, plus at least one independent corroborator (a CLOSED circle audit or a present artifact). No passing fixture, no completed verdict -- inspection alone can never settle it
a fixture that could not be run to a verdict is INCONCLUSIVE, recorded as neither a pass nor a fail; and any non-passing fixture blocks a COMPLETED verdict whatever else is present

APPEND-ONLY: the original dispatch rows are never rewritten or deleted. A disposition is a new forward record in runtime/orphan-dispositions.jsonl citing `resolves_dispatch_id`; re-running a sweep appends again and readers take latest-wins

A WORK VERDICT IS NOT A COST MEASUREMENT. This circle writes no cost field; runCostTotal.js keeps reporting an orphan `unmeasured` unless a real measurement exists on the row, and its disposition input is display-only

reported ONCE with counts through the operator channel, grouped by CAUSE and never one line per row. A cause key names a cause and never carries a dispatch id, lug name or timestamp -- a key with a coordinate in it makes every occurrence its own cause
no lug is filed by this mechanism. A lug is a unit of work someone owes; a verdict is information, and information is reported, not filed as work

circles.name: oversized-canon-write-guard
invariants: counts tokens with the compiler's own tokenizer (o200k_base) against rule 11's own PER_FILE_TOKEN_CAP -- imported, never restated -- so write-time and compile-time can never disagree

measures with rule 11's own measureCanonContent: on a lug file the verb-owned bookkeeping (VERB_OWNED_LUG_FIELDS, declared once in the rule) is excluded, so the guard, the compile rule and the verb hold the same authored contract to the cap
refuses with the measured count, the cap, the file and the fix path; never truncates or edits the content
scope is rule 11's scope: a kind-bearing yaml entity file, its instructions_ref target, or a doc a sibling yaml names as instructions_ref -- a loader skip dir is never checked
a write over the cap but strictly smaller than the file already on disk is allowed as progress and announced, not refused
Bash writes are not measured here -- disclosed; compile remains the backstop
consumers: external:wcl-verify-then-launch (a doc this guard refuses never reaches the operator as a launch-time hygiene report)

circles.name: pattern-language
invariants: ONE VOCABULARY, IN THE GLOSSARY. The terms live as a section of canon/glossary.md in its what/why/where shape, parsed mechanically; there is no second glossary. Every term's *Where:* pointer must resolve on disk, and a term that stops resolving is reported untraced, never rounded up
VALUE AND LIFT ARE SEPARATE. Value is purpose (what/why) and is never a number. Lift is measured improvement over a REAL baseline. An unmeasurable lift reads `unmeasured` -- never zero, never a guess

LIFT IS A SUCCESS_PREDICTION, NOT A NEW SHAPE. A declared lift registers with subject_kind `pattern` through the same gates every advisor's prediction passes: no reader, unfalsifiable, trivially safe, no baseline without first_baseline -- each refuses the declaration and writes nothing

DECLARE AT CREATION; DERIVE WHEN MISSING. A pattern with no declared value or lift gets both DERIVED from its own attempts on the record (distinct-subject success rate against every other approach at its problem class), marked `derived` with the attempt ids. A spoke's lift derives from its own dispatch history, later half against earlier half, below ten rows per half unmeasured

EVERY FIGURE CARRIES ITS ORIGIN: declared | derived | asserted | unmeasured, with a provenance pointer. A self-description's fields are derived from named repository files or asserted from local/design-assertions.json, and the tally is printed first
THE EXISTING LEVEL ENUM, NO NEW AXIS. Descriptions carry `spoke`; views carry `group` or `wheel`; the enum is read from schemas/common.schema.json, and a level outside it is refused

A VARIANT STATES ITS VARIATION. derived_from with no variation and rationale is refused as a retry wearing a new name; a dangling or self predecessor and a lineage cycle are refused, on the same index lugs use

A CORRECTION CARRIES THIRD-PARTY EVIDENCE: a chain disposition on disk reading `closed`, whose witness is independent of the declarer by checkIndependence. Self-certification is refused; a missing, seek_refresh or deprecated chain is refused
NO LUG IS FILED to convey a description, a pattern or a lift figure. Artifacts land under generated/ and a ledger row reports them

circles.name: pickup-time-reverification
invariants: it runs at pickup and only at pickup -- there is no sweep, no schedule, and no reader of the dispatch registry in the mechanism, so an in-flight dispatch is never killed by it
only a positive "not needed" stops a pickup; where real state cannot answer, the verdict is unknown and the work proceeds with that recorded
no premise-validity oracle is invented -- a positive premise answer claims only that nothing in real state contradicts the premise, never that the premise is true
a stop is never silent: the verdict lands on the lug file, in the ledger, and (on the dispatch path) on a refused registry row naming the reason
a lug stopped at pickup leaves the ready queue carrying its recorded reason, rather than being re-offered and re-refused forever
only "deprecated" stops work; "closed" and "seek_refresh" are reported as unknown with the disposition named, because the settled vocabulary does not say what either means for a specific pickup
a disposition row with no certified_by cannot stop work -- a chain cannot self-certify its way to a stop

circles.name: planner-cross-segment-ranking
invariants: ONE ranked queue, build and maintain alike: initiative membership is the first-order key -- every row belonging to a live AP-ready initiative ranks ahead of every row that belongs to none, and the initiative is named on the row; operator-declared priority governs INSIDE each tier, never across them (the operator's 260911 decision on the comparable impact unit, verbatim on the artifact)

a maintain row is affiliated with an initiative when that initiative's consumers names the advisor (initiative.consumers -> initiativeAdvisorIndex); a build row when the initiative's lugs names the lug (initiativeLugIndex); an IN-DESIGN or non-live initiative affiliates nothing

sequencing is honoured inside the initiative tier: work for an initiative sequenced_after an unlanded one ranks below the one it waits on, and the row carries waiting_on and sequencingBlock's own reason; a prerequisite that is not declared is reported, never treated as landed

a declared guaranteed_runtime_share floor is reserved off the top in computeAdvisorAllocation BEFORE ranking, and rankCrossSegment never moves a share -- a floored advisor ranked last still holds its floor

no price is invented for a build row: share stays null with the reason stated; remaining capacity is measured as the maintain share not held by initiative-tier rows plus a COUNT of build slots, never a fabricated fraction
the existing refusal on an unparseable advisor file is neither dropped nor reordered: the cycle then carries build rows only, still ranked, with zero maintain runtime stated

cross_segment_ranking reads ranked with cross_segment_ranking_rule initiative_membership_first; the planner-conductor-impact prediction (planner_cross_segment_ranking_ranked, baseline 0) is the live proof and is never edited to match

circles.name: planner-cycle-allocation
invariants: a declared guaranteed_runtime_share floor is reserved off the top before any weighting, so weighting can only ADD to it -- and the result is asserted against the floor again before it is returned; Planner may never reduce a floor
an advisor file that cannot be read makes Planner REFUSE to emit any shares at all, naming the file and the parse error -- it never allocates around a roster it could not fully read
only advisors that are status: live AND declare a real autopilot_budget_ms receive a share; every exclusion is named, never silent

build rows are ranked but NEVER priced (share: null) -- no measurement prices a lug against an advisor's runtime share; the operator's 260911 decision made initiative membership the ranking key (planner-cross-segment-ranking), not a price
no LLM call, no network: the cycle is real arithmetic over real recorded dispatch history, deterministic given the same roster and ledger
an allocatable advisor that receives a zero share this cycle is reported by name in zero_share_advisors -- starvation is a finding, never a rounding artifact
the persisted cycle declares its own max_age_ms and a consumer reports it as stale past that bound rather than trusting it as current

circles.name: precompact-checkpoint
invariants: never blocks the compaction -- exits 0 even when the checkpoint dir is unwritable or nothing is active
never overwrites a prior checkpoint for the same session -- one file per real PreCompact firing, timestamped
the rotation duty never replaces the checkpoint duty -- both run on the same firing, in separate try/catch blocks, checkpoint first
rotation never truncates or deletes real history -- the closed segment keeps every decision, transition and direction it had, and stays on disk under runtime/track-segments/<session_id>/
rotation preserves session identity -- the fresh track carries the same session_id, identity_triple and turn_ordinal, so it is the same session's NEXT file, not a new session
rotation leaves runtime/tracks/ with exactly one file per session, so every existing directory-walking reader (archiveOldTracks, minder's /wheel-ops readTracks) is unaffected
the review pass reads the ONE canon phrase list (canon/disclosed-gap-phrases.yaml) and never auto-files or auto-dismisses a finding -- a human or Max decides
rotation refuses rather than half-acts on an already-closed track -- session-end owns that close

circles.name: process-signal-inbox
invariants: a message is never evaluated as an instruction -- its fields are stringified into a ledger row's text, never executed or used to select a code path
a message routed once is never routed again -- tracked by name, not position, so one stuck message never blocks the ones after it
a message this run could not route stays counted in inbox depth and is named, with a reason, rather than silently skipped

circles.name: provider-usage-and-retry
invariants: ONE ROW PER ATTEMPT in runtime/provider-usage.jsonl -- successes, refusals, timeouts, retried attempts and calls blocked by a ceiling all write a row; an absence in that file means no call was made, and nothing else

the record is written unconditionally, NOT through observability/eventLog.js, because appendEvent refuses to write with no announced session triple -- which is exactly the headless-verifier case this circle exists for

usage is what the provider itself reported: prompt/completion tokens from the OpenAI-compatible usage block or the claude CLI's input/output/modelUsage shape, and NULL -- never zero -- when the provider reported nothing
error_kind distinguishes rate_limited (429), auth (401/403), server (>=500) and http_error (everything else); a 401 and a 503 are never the same word again
bounded retry, same provider only -- the contract never falls back to a different provider, so a check is always answered by the provider the caller named or by nobody

retry is attempted only for the kinds the lug's acceptance names (rate_limited, server). RETRY_ON_TIMEOUT is a single constant, currently false, carrying a documented operator decision pending: the incident that opened the lug was a TIMEOUT
backoff is bounded exponential (500ms doubling, capped at 30s) and honours a provider's own Retry-After when it sent one, itself capped by the same ceiling
the result carries attempts and retry_history, so a caller that got a thin answer can see it was thin
