NO REAL CEILING IS SHIPPED for any provider: canon/provider-ceilings.yaml ships with an empty providers map, because no quota or pricing figure has been verified from real config
a ceiling carrying a number but no source: is REFUSED rather than enforced -- the call proceeds and the refusal is stated; a limit nobody can trace is not a limit
a declared, sourced ceiling blocks the call BEFORE any request is sent, and writes both an attempt row and a ledger row naming the number and its source

unmeasured is never exhausted: a provider whose calls reported no usage, or that has no rows at all, is never blocked -- a wrongly blocked verification silently thins a review, which is the failure this circle exists to end
the ceiling gate can never block by failing: any error inside it allows the call and says why
NO SECRET IS EVER RECORDED -- a usage record names the provider and the cost, never the credential; free text carried from a provider's own error body is redacted first

circles.name: publish-kb-cut
invariants: kb/capabilities-graph.md is never written to by this circle -- read-only, one direction, hub to spoke
a spoke's received cut carries a checksum (cut_checksum) computed over the real content file (cut_source_path), verified again at that spoke's own next compile (admission rule 18, kb-cut-integrity)
a registered spoke's repo that cannot be read is reported as unreadable, never silently skipped
a spoke is never written to unless explicitly opted in for this run -- writing into a live spoke's repo it was never asked to touch is not this circle's call to make unilaterally

circles.name: raw-session-snapshot-end
invariants: only the NEW bytes of the raw log are copied; the stored segments concatenate to the source prefix and history is never re-stored
a segment the credential gate refuses is held back locally and recorded with its range and hash; the next segment still lands
a spoke whose remote is public or unreadable keeps segments local (runtime/sessions-local) with a recorded finding
growth is bounded by the per-spoke session_record budget in file-size-budgets, warned before it is reached
raw content never reaches a model provider; only counts, ranges and hashes are reported
consumers: external:track-generation (the said and considered track is built from these segments)
external:session-exit-commit (runtime/sessions is a tier-1 runtime path, committed with the spoke)

growth is bounded by the per-spoke session_record budget in file-size-budgets, warned before it is reached

circles.name: raw-worktree-add-redirect
invariants: heuristic, not a parser -- a `git [-C dir] [-c k=v] worktree add` at a command position; a quoted mention or a grep for the phrase is not a match
the refusal names the registrar verb (node scripts/worktree.js add ...) built from the refused command's own path, branch and ref
the registrar itself runs git through spawnSync, never through a session's Bash tool, so it is never refused
consumers: external:operator (every harness worktree carries an owner, purpose and expiry, so the worktree gc can tell a live tree from an abandoned one)

circles.name: readiness-certification-sweep
invariants: EVERY REACHED LUG GETS A RECORDED RESULT: one runtime/readiness-sweep.jsonl row per lug with a disposition (done | left_at_review | left_at_ready), a reason AND the refusing gate by name (refused_by). A lug with no fixture is recorded as `no fixture to re-run`; a closed gate quotes the gate; a verb refusal is quoted verbatim. Nothing is skipped silently and nothing is rubber-stamped

DONE ONLY THROUGH THE KERNEL VERB, ONLY ON A FIXTURE RE-RUN GREEN NOW: the lug's own fixture is resolved (its `// lug:` marker across instance and framework repos, plus its tests: entries) and EXECUTED by this sweep; red never reaches the verb; a declared test file missing on disk is INCONCLUSIVE, never trusted. The verb's refusal is the verdict -- no pre_attribution_flag row, no hand edit, no gate weakened

NEVER runProofer WITHOUT certifyOnly: a Proofer PASS moves review -> ready and would drag merged work back into the ready queue. Certification happens only through scripts/cross-provider-certify.js (policy run), the detached requester the initiative drive uses (policy request), or not at all (policy none, the default)

THE TALLY IS RENDERED FROM THE ROWS, NEVER HAND-KEPT: N reviewed = M done + K left at review, with reasons ranked by class; the tally doc section between the TALLY markers is re-rendered after every lug so a kill mid-sweep loses at most the lug in flight

A SPENT BUDGET STOPS THE SWEEP: on the wall-clock budget or --max-lugs it stops before the next lug, names every unreached lug in `not_reached`, counts none of them as reviewed, and the CLI exits 3 -- a truncated sweep is never read as a complete one

WRITES ONLY ITS OWN EVIDENCE: the stream, the pointed tally doc, one ledger row per run. Lug files change only through the verb; certification records only through the certifier. --dry-run writes nothing

A PROOFER PASS IS NEVER INVISIBLE: the sweep enumerates ready+passed (the Proofer's post-PASS shape), never ready+stubbed. ONE PROMOTE PATH: donePromotion.js promoteLugToDone is the only body that reads the gate and asks the verb for done, for the sweep and the initiative drive alike
no lug is filed by this mechanism. A left-at-review reason is information, reported in the tally; a lug is opened only for a real remediation owed

circles.name: ready-gate-stub
invariants: never mutates the lug it checks
never allows readiness: passed -- only readiness: stubbed can enter ready until increment 7
every stubbed entry into ready writes a ledger row; it never passes silently

circles.name: reconcile-advisor-roster
invariants: reconciliation proposes; it never deletes an advisor contract on its own
an advisor present in a spoke but absent from the canonical roster produces a ledger row rather than being silently adopted
a spoke whose advisors cannot be read is reported as unreadable, never silently skipped

inside a readable spoke, an individual unparseable *.advisor.yaml is reported by file name with its parse error, never silently dropped -- and that spoke's other, valid advisor files are still reconciled

circles.name: reconcile-ledger
invariants: never mutates an existing ledger row; proposals only, plus additive counter-metric rows each run
deterministic given the same ledger and canon snapshot

circles.name: regression-oracle
invariants: every oracle's pass/fail is a real, deterministic command's real exit code -- no model/LLM anywhere in the verdict
a capability's last_green {ts, sha} is never discarded on a red run -- only overwritten by a later real pass, so a red row still answers 'when did this last work'
a capability that has never once passed is reported red, never regression -- REGRESSION is reserved for was-green-now-red, distinct from always-been-broken
the ledger is read fresh and rewritten whole each run -- never recomputed from nothing, never partially patched

the sweep runs OFF the wheel-clock lease: the job launches scripts/regression-oracle-sweep.mjs detached under its own liveness-judged lease (one sweep at a time, at most once per declared cadence) and reports the last COMPLETED sweep's verdict, never a guess about one in flight

circles.name: release-policy
invariants: NEVER A PUSH NOBODY CHOSE: under ask nothing is pushed until the operator picks smoke or full; exit-push is refused unless the policy is push_every_exit; a spoke with no policy file is ask with an empty smoke list

AN EMPTY SMOKE LIST IS A GAP, NEVER A GREEN: smoke with no smoke_suites is refused naming the gap; smoke runs exactly the declared suites through the gate's own runSuites, and any red, timed-out or unreached suite means nothing is folded and nothing pushed
THE FULL SUITE IS NEVER RUN UNASKED AT EXIT: exit-push runs no suite; it folds and pushes with WHEEL_SKIP_TEST_GATE naming the policy and records the session's last test run

ONE BYPASS PATH: smoke and exit-push push through the gate's existing, ledgered WHEEL_SKIP_TEST_GATE with a reason naming policy, level, smoke counts and sha; full is a plain push so the pre-push full gate runs
FAST-FORWARD ONLY: the session branch is folded into main with git fetch . <branch>:main only when main is its ancestor; a non-fast-forward is refused and named, never merged or forced
EVERY OUTCOME IS ONE `release` LEDGER ROW naming policy, level, suite result, and the sha pushed or the reason nothing was
A SMOKE RELEASE PUSHES TO ORIGIN ONLY; a framework cut to the fleet still needs a full green run (hf deploy's cut stage, unchanged)
COMPILE REFUSES AN INVALID POLICY: rule 23 applies the command's own releasePolicyProblems -- an unknown release_policy or a smoke entry naming no real file

circles.name: rule-12-live-state-report
invariants: every block a SessionStart hook injects declares itself canon or live at its composer (src/lugTracking/injectionDerivation.js); the rule never infers a part's derivation from its text
the refusal sums the canon-derived parts only -- two compiles of one unchanged canon give one verdict, whatever runtime/ and ledger/ hold

the live parts are measured exactly as before and reported as a compile warning when the whole injection is over the cap, with the total, the canon/live split and every live section's own number -- never hidden, never a refusal, and the cap is never raised for it

every live-growing section carries a declared count cap and a "+N more, see <store>" tail at its composer; the hook and the rule read one composer each, so the injected text and the measured text are the same string
upkeep-miss, footer-miss and vetoable-act rows shrink only through the one acknowledge path, with a reason, status set on the row and nothing deleted; no reason, no acknowledgement

circles.name: run-roi-extraction
invariants: a run cannot end without an extraction: the launch path, the decline path and the abnormal-end path all reach it, and a run that throws still produces one marked complete: false rather than none
every KPI names where its number came from, and a KPI that could not be measured carries value null with state "unmeasured" -- never a zero, because a zero is a claim
no caller can hand the extractor a verdict: every KPI is backed by an artifact written by a different process than the run being evaluated, and a KPI with no corroborating artifact stays unmeasured
a dispatch the run CLAIMS succeeded with no advisor-dispatch ledger twin is counted as unrecorded and reported, never promoted into a measured success
the remediation decision is always explicit -- a named cause with the evidence and the declared threshold it crossed, or "none owed" with a stated reason per rule
every cause key names a CAUSE and never a per-event coordinate, so N occurrences of one fault collapse to one finding; a cause already named by an open lug is reported, not re-filed

at most one remediation lug is filed per run, strongest evidence first; every other owed cause is REPORTED on the wave record and in the operator channel, so the mechanism cannot flood the backlog by construction
a filed remediation lug reaches `defined` through the kernel verb's own admission gate, never by a direct state write
the extraction rides on the wave record the run already opened -- one stream, one shape -- and is a declared data point in WAVE_RECORD_DATA_POINTS with its own gatherer, consumer and staleness age

the steering damps WHICH spoke a wave goes to and can never turn a launch into a no-launch; a spoke's factor is at most 1.00, so no run can raise its own spoke's weight on its own extraction, and it is floored so no amount of damping drives a spoke to nothing

the per-run history read is bounded to a tail and says so; only the scheduled reconciliation sweep reads the whole stream, and it leaves its count where the wave-never-closed rule reads it, so a leak older than the tail is counted, never invisible

a wave opened more than one five-hour window ago with no closed row is closed EXPLICITLY as unrecoverable, with an unmeasured outcome naming why and reconciled: true -- never with a guessed result and never left silent
the operator channel reports causes with counts and is SILENT when nothing is owed

circles.name: scheduler-failure-operator-channel
invariants: a job failing on consecutive ticks reaches the operator -- never a ledger row alone
one notification per streak, per job, never one per failing tick
a success resets the streak, so the next real run of failures announces again
the same job failing a genuinely different way announces again -- a new class is a new finding
the session-start surface reports failure CLASSES with counts and first/last-seen, never one line per failing row
a class an open lug already names is reported as known, with that lug's name, not re-reported as new
only jobs in a live streak surface -- a class that stopped happening disappears on its own
streaks and classes are derived from the real ledger rows, never from a second counter that could drift from them
an undeliverable toast (no transport, posture off, headless) is disclosed with its real reason and still leaves the durable ledger row
the channel never throws past its own boundary -- a broken operator channel must not take down the wheel clock

circles.name: secrets-template-migration
invariants: THE TEMPLATE IS THE MANIFEST'S INPUT, NEVER DISCARDED: migrate derives canon/secrets.manifest.yaml from .env.template (#@secret + #@optional lines; a #@seed-from annotation or an op:// value verbatim as vault/item/field; a key with neither gets item=<spoke>, field=<KEY>, needs_op_item: true); the template is byte-identical after, asserted by sha256

A MANIFEST THAT EXISTS IS NEVER OVERWRITTEN: a changed template yields canon/secrets.manifest.yaml.v2-proposed (the regenerate-docs proposal discipline); an unchanged template (same sha256) yields nothing -- idempotent, zero-cost

DUAL-READ FOR THE MIGRATION CYCLE: getSecret reads the resolved cache first and falls back to the template's own op:// reference through the one existing resolver (onePassword.js), writing exactly ONE ledger decision row per fallback, attribution secrets-template-fallback, naming the key and the path -- never a value

RETIREMENT IS PER SPOKE AND MEASURED, NEVER GLOBAL: only when the manifest's own migrated_at is max_age x 7 in the past AND zero fallback rows landed inside that window does applyCut rename .env.template to .env.template.migrated-<cut> and record its sha256 in migrated_from. Never deleted. An unobserved window is not a zero

1PASSWORD STAYS THE SOURCE OF TRUTH; NO VALUE IS EVER WRITTEN to canon, a manifest, a proposal, a ledger row, a log line or a fixture output -- the resolver writes only .local/secrets.json (mode 600, gitignored)
ORGANIC SPREAD: the schema, the migrate tool, the step-5 hook and the dual-read ship in the cut; a spoke learns them through update-discovery and applyCut alone -- no session is told, no hand step

circles.name: session-continuity-checkpoint
invariants: never blocks session start
the active lug loads in full; the rest of the backlog loads as one-line summaries
silent when nothing is in flight and the backlog is empty

circles.name: session-end-handoff
invariants: every real session end produces exactly one handoff
the track is closed (closed_at set) exactly once, with the same handoff

circles.name: session-end-notify
invariants: best-effort only -- a failed or unavailable toast transport never blocks a real session close
no transport means no notification, never a synthetic/logged stand-in claimed as a real one
consumers: external:operator (real-time awareness that a session closed, without watching the terminal)

circles.name: session-exit-commit
invariants: the staged set is only this session's own files (its files-touched record unioned with its transcript's tool_use blocks) plus the hook-written harness state, by pathspec -- never `git add -A`; a file a live peer lane also touched is contended and left with a row naming both ids; a file this session never touched is left and named for its lane, or as unattributed; a commit that cannot attribute stays scoped, never widens (lug session-exit-commit-sweeps-a-peer-lanes-in-flight-files, 260914)
no commit ever contains credential material: rule 13's credential patterns run over the staged set first, and a finding blocks the commit and unstages

a red aggregator never reaches the mainline: the work lands on a wip/* branch, unpushed, with a ledger row and a stderr line that both name the branch and the verb that consumes it (`hf deploy --stage fold`)
never --force and never --no-verify: a rejected push and a refusing hook are both reported, never overridden
the commit message is generated from the session's real track -- coordinates, lug transitions, prompt ids -- never typed
a push that fails leaves the commit local and is announced at the next wakeup's what-changed

a refused commit is surfaced, never silent: the hook prints the refusal verdict to stderr and exits non-zero so Claude Code shows it, and the ledger row carries the verdict line intact -- never the first 500 characters of gate chatter

the hook's timeout is derived from measurement (hook_timeout_seconds: 60 = Claude Code's observed cancel window, three real /exit's on 2026-09-14 cancelled at ~60s whatever was declared), never a round default

every run prints exactly one verdict line on stderr, last (`session-exit-commit: <repo>: committed N file(s) as <sha8>, push deferred (<why>) | clean | REFUSED -- <cause> | push failed -- <cause> | wip <branch> <sha8> (tree was red)`) and writes the same verdict to runtime/exit-verdict.json {session_id, repo, verdict, detail, at, wall_ms}, the file wcl's closed: line reads, never the ledger tail (lug exit-prints-one-verdict-line, 260916)

SessionEnd never runs the full suite: the commit gate gets a fixed 12s budget (EXIT_GATE_BUDGET_MS) and DEFERS the suites it cannot reach to the push gate by name; the push is never attempted at exit (a deferral row, announced next wakeup); a repo reached after the 45s wall cap is DEFERRED with a row, never started -- the hook always returns inside Claude Code's window with every row written

circles.name: session-files-touched
invariants: one row per path the finished call wrote to, keyed by the session (and the fork's agent_id when present) that made it, in runtime/files-touched/<session_id>.jsonl under the session's cwd
targets are the write-scope guard's own extraction (writeTargetsForTool, src/lugTracking/dispatchScope.js) -- one extractor for 'what does this call write', never a second
a read-shaped call records nothing: no row, no file created

circles.name: stop-turn-marker
invariants: one marker per turn, tagged with whichever lug was active

nothing is auto-filed and nothing is auto-closed -- a finding stays open until a human or Max names a lug or a dismissal reason (hf gap-findings resolve)
a phrase already carried by a real lug, or written into lugs/, ledger/ or runtime/ or into this mechanism's own files, is suppressed with its reason -- the same gap is never double-filed
this is an additional, narrower signal: reference aging (warmup-goals-review's REFERENCES AGED block) is neither read nor replaced here

circles.name: success-prediction
invariants: a prediction is registered BEFORE the work and immutable after: the registry is append-only with no update path; a change is a superseding row that never rewrites the original
superseding is REFUSED once any verdict exists or check_by has passed -- editing the target to match the result is the failure mode this circle exists to prevent -- and a refusal writes nothing

canon DECLARES a prediction so it is machine-readable, but canon is not the bar: the registered row carries a digest, verdicts are judged against it, and a later canon edit is reported as divergence, not absorbed

a prediction is accepted only when certified FALSIFIABLE by canon/circles/falsifiability-gate.yaml's standard -- the verdict really moved on a mutated mirror of the observation swept across the metric's domain, never on its wording; no finite domain is UNPROVEN and refused, and one no observation could SATISFY is refused alongside one none could refute

a trivially-safe prediction is refused with its class named -- already true at the baseline, or near-vacuous (90%+ of the domain satisfies it); no measured baseline is refused unless first_baseline: true is declared

the review is by a THIRD PARTY or not at all: the registrant and every recorded executor session are refused, the reviewer must pass the four-axis src/advisor/independence.js check, and the clock grades only as the calling session. A refusal writes nothing
the verdict has THREE outcomes -- achieved, missed, unevaluable -- and unevaluable is never scored as either: the achieved rate's denominator is achieved+missed only
no reader substitutes a zero for an absent measurement: a reading is a real number, or value null with a reason; a reader that throws is reported, never swallowed

a MISSED prediction triggers a real deeper review -- the gap, whether the metric moved at all from its baseline, prior misses -- and opens ONE remediation lug through the kernel verb, on the same cause key the ROI extractor's branch dedupes on
NO LUG IS EVER FILED TO REPORT A VERDICT: N verdicts become ONE operator-channel section with counts, silent when nothing is owed; only a real owed remediation becomes a lug

every cause key names a CAUSE (subject kind, subject, metric), never a per-event coordinate -- no session id, run id, date or timestamp -- so N occurrences collapse to one finding; at most one lug per sweep, the rest REPORTED
a subject whose prediction is unevaluable three times running is surfaced as a finding against its own DEFINITION -- an unmeasurable counter_metric is a defect, not a neutral outcome

circles.name: temporary-limit-boost-awareness
invariants: the four statuses are never collapsed: announced (a real notice in a fresh flag cache), lapsed (a real notice past its own stated expiry), absent (a fresh cache carrying no notice -- the only real negative), unknown (no readable cache, no age stamp, or a cache older than MAX_FLAG_CACHE_AGE_HOURS)

a boost is NEVER inferred from a utilization percentage, from a generous-looking headroom figure, or from any flag that does not itself state a boosted bar -- there is exactly one path to `announced` and it is a real notice a reader can go and look at

the notice text is carried through verbatim on every fact, and magnitude/expiry are populated only on a strict pattern match against the notice's own words; a notice that stops matching yields nulls with a named reason rather than a guessed number
the year and timezone absent from the notice text are resolved by a disclosed rule and reported as expiry_precision: day with the assumptions listed -- never presented as a provider-declared instant

pacing rescales no percentage: a boost's only effect is to shorten the deadline a runway is measured to, to min(window reset, conservative boost expiry), on the provider's own unmodified utilization figures
a notice naming the five_hour bar is REFUSED by the pace model and the refusal disclosed -- the five-hour Envelope's conservative posture may never weaken to buy opportunistic speed
only status `announced` changes pacing; unknown, absent and lapsed leave every pace figure bit-identical to the pre-boost behaviour
the expiry signal fires on the earlier (conservative) expiry bound and on every heartbeat outcome including declines, so a boost is surfaced before it lapses rather than after
read-only: the flag cache and the usage reading are read, never written, refreshed or rotated
consumers: external:operator (the headless poller's own boost line)

circles.name: turn-failure-record

NO MESSAGE CONTENT ANYWHERE: the payload's message fields are read in memory to classify and dropped; the row holds no prompt, reply, command text or file path, and the live capture is handed the payload with those fields withheld

THE TASK RESUMES, THE CONTENT DOES NOT: the next UserPromptSubmit (turn-start-attribution) or SessionStart (warmup-goals-review) of that session injects one block -- class and time, active lug, the files written in the stopped turn with their present state, the last operator ask from the turn record, the sanctioned scripts -- and acknowledges the row with an appended row, so it is injected once; nothing rewords or resends a stopped message
MEASURED: the session start prints TURN FAILURES with the 7-day count by class, silent at zero
NEVER BLOCKS AND NEVER FAILS A TURN: exit 0 on every path, no stdout, a failure inside the body is swallowed; the resume block and the session-start line return null instead of throwing

circles.name: unattended-run-kill-switch
invariants: FAIL SAFE, the load-bearing rule: if the stop file cannot be READ for any reason, that is a STOP, not a go. A clean ENOENT on a readable instance root is the only reading that permits unattended spend. A wrong stop costs a declined wave, recorded and visible; a wrong go keeps spending an absent operator's quota through the exact fault that made the switch unreadable.

it halts BOTH halves or it is not a kill switch: new launches at the next gate AND every already-running child, through its recorded pids. Halting new launches while running dispatches keep spending is the failure this closes, not a partial success.
a halted tick consumes nothing -- no reading, no reconciliation, above all no five-hour window boundary -- so clearing the flag restores the wheel to exactly where it was

a child terminated by the stop switch is recorded `killed`, never `timed_out`: a session the operator halted did not run too long, and calling it a timeout sends the morning reader hunting a watchdog bug that is not there

the file IS the interface: `touch runtime/stop.flag` from any shell halts the wheel completely, with no node and no working harness. The JSON body `hf stop` writes is a courtesy; an empty hand-touched file is a full stop. The CLI exists only because it can ALSO reach running children and queued rows.

the halt is fault-isolated: a killPendingDispatches failure (unresolvable counterparty, unloadable canon) is reported honestly and does NOT prevent the flag going up or children being signalled -- a kill switch that refuses to halt because it could not load a YAML file is an elaborate way of not having one
process liveness is CHECKED with signal 0, never inferred from a missing 'ended' row: a SIGKILLed supervisor never writes one, and a recycled pid must never be signalled on a stranger's behalf
cost is SUMMED FROM REAL TURN MARKERS ONLY -- never estimated, never priced, never defaulted to zero. A dispatch whose cost was not really measured reports `unmeasured`.
every whole-run total is three numbers, not one: the measured sum, how many dispatches it covers, and how many it does NOT. A confident wrong number is worse than an honest gap.
consumers: external:operator (`hf stop`, `hf stop --status`, and the morning warmup's run-cost section)
external:minder (the dispatch registry's per-row cost fields, which the Conductor-waves view reads)
